clue.text: Avoid outskirts of coastal town? OK

indicators.note: to avoid the outskirts is to drop the first and last letters of the town's name

parts.note: Brighton is a seaside town on England's south coast

explanation.surface: Someone agrees, a little grudgingly, to steer clear of the edge of a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Avoid outskirts of' strips B and N, the first and last letters, from BRIGHTON, a resort on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are casual British expressions of agreement, an informal 'all right'.

clue.text: Criticise highly-rated financial institutions for greed

parts.note: to rap is to rebuke or criticise
A is a top rating, as in A1 or an A grade
the City is London's financial district, home to its banks

explanation.surface: Someone attacks top-rated banks for their avarice.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is the financial district of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapacity is grasping, insatiable avarice.

clue.text: Jokes about youngster needing right clothes for special occasion

indicators.note: about means around, so the jokes word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: gags are jokes
a lad is a boy, a youngster

explanation.surface: A boy needs the right outfit for a party, but people mock him.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad rags is an informal term for one's best outfit worn to a party.

clue.text: Plant is brown with silvery edges

parts.note: tan is a yellowish-brown colour

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A plant described as brown with silver margins on its leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with silvery edges' takes S and Y, the first and last letters of 'silvery'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tansy is a yellow-flowered herb of the daisy family.

clue.text: The tanks are rolling in Asian capital

indicators.note: tanks rolling in suggests the letters of the phrase tumbling into a new order

explanation.surface: Armoured vehicles advance into a Central Asian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are rolling' shuffles THE TANKS into the city's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Tashkent is the capital city of Uzbekistan in Central Asia.

clue.text: A leading role given to unknown? That introduces troubles in play

indicators.note: introduces means brings something inside, so troubles goes into the phrase before it

parts.note: a big part is a leading role
ails as a verb means troubles
y is a standard algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: An unknown actor gets the lead in a drama full of difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: A BIG PART Y is built first, then 'introduces' puts AILS after A BIG. Abigail's Party is Mike Leigh's 1977 suburban comedy of manners.
explanation.definitionFit: Abigail's Party is a celebrated stage and television drama by Mike Leigh.

clue.text: Country house: we'll be entertained in one decorated for a celebration

parts.note: a hall is a large country house

indicators.note: to be entertained in something is to be a guest inside it, so one piece goes within another
decorated suggests the word one is dressed up, its letters rearranged

parts.note: we'll is short for we will, so the word we is what gets entertained

explanation.surface: Guests at a stately home will be hosted in a room dressed up for a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decorated' turns ONE into OEN; 'be entertained in' puts WE (from we'll, read as 'we will') inside, giving OWEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Halloween is the October 31 festival of costumes and trick-or-treating.

clue.text: Start to exercise long before nine: Irish remedy

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: IX is nine in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A tonic for the Irish: get up and exercise early, before nine o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: An elixir is a medicinal potion, supposedly a cure-all.

clue.text: Given nickname when caught during game

definitions.meaning: labelled with an alternative name or tag
touched by the chaser in the playground chasing game

explanation.surface: A child gets a nickname after being caught in a playground game.
explanation.definitionFit: To be tagged is to be labelled, and also to be touched out in the game of tag.

clue.text: Into empty pan put uncooked seafood

indicators.note: into says the next piece is placed inside the emptied pan
an empty pan keeps only its first and last letters, its contents gone

parts.note: uncooked food is raw

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction: put the raw seafood into an empty pan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves P and N from 'pan'; 'Into' puts RAW between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A prawn is a small shellfish eaten as seafood.

clue.text: Concealing diamonds in temporary shelter

indicators.note: in places the diamonds inside the shelter word

parts.note: a shieling is a rough hut used by shepherds in summer pastures
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: Gems hidden away in a makeshift hut.
explanation.walkthrough: A SHIELING is a Scottish and northern English word for a herdsman's summer hut; 'in' puts D (diamonds) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Shielding something from view is screening or hiding it.

clue.text: In road near Tennessee spot tiny flowers

indicators.note: in says the tiny word is placed inside the road word

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a road
wee is Scottish for small or tiny
Tennessee Williams was the American playwright

explanation.surface: Someone notices small blooms on a street close to the state of Tennessee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tennessee' looks like the US state; it is the playwright Tennessee Williams. 'In' puts WEE inside ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet williams are a garden pink, Dianthus barbatus, with clustered blooms.

clue.text: Writer read out passage by Marx, perhaps

indicators.note: read out says the pieces are spoken and the spelling follows the sound

parts.note: Karl Marx gives KARL, and a passage between seats is an aisle, so Marx's passage is Karl's aisle

explanation.surface: Someone recites an extract from the writings of Karl Marx.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' flags Marx as one example of a Karl; KARL + AISLE spoken aloud gives the Scottish essayist Thomas Carlyle.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Carlyle was a Victorian Scottish historian and essayist, an author.

clue.text: Plant — source of annoyance once it spreads

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, its first letter
spreads suggests the letters fanning out into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A weed becomes a nuisance as soon as it starts to spread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'source of' gives A, the first letter of 'annoyance'; 'spreads' rearranges ONCE IT into CONITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Aconite, also called monkshood or wolfsbane, is a poisonous flowering perennial.

clue.text: Fancy galette? All I wanted is plain pasta

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or ornamental, so the following letters are decorated into a new order

explanation.surface: A diner turns down an elaborate French pastry, wanting only simple noodles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like a verb or an adjective for the galette; it rearranges GALETTE + ALL + I.
explanation.definitionFit: Tagliatelle is long flat ribbon noodles, a basic Italian dish.

clue.text: In most of island workers secured wage rise

indicators.note: secured means held fast, so the island part holds the workers inside
most of a word is all of it but the last letter

parts.note: Crete is a Greek island
men are workers, as in hands or staff

explanation.surface: On a large island, labour won a pay increase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims CRETE to CRET; 'secured' puts MEN inside, giving CREMENT after IN.
explanation.definitionFit: An increment is a step up in pay on a salary scale.

clue.text: Maybe bitter about dictator supporting college application

indicators.note: about means around, so the beer word goes around the dictator

parts.note: bitter is a kind of beer, an example of ale, hence maybe
Idi Amin was the dictator of Uganda

explanation.surface: Perhaps a beer drinker talks about a tyrant backing a university application.
explanation.walkthrough: 'application' looks like a form; it is a lotion you apply. In a down answer 'supporting' sets ALAMINE below C.
explanation.definitionFit: Calamine is a pink lotion applied to soothe itchy or sunburnt skin.

clue.text: Thin person that trains runners

definitions.meaning: a tall stick up which runner beans are grown

explanation.surface: A lanky athletics coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runners' looks like athletes; they are runner beans, trained up a pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A beanpole is slang for a tall thin person, and literally a pole supporting climbing beans.

clue.text: Type of furniture stripper

definitions.meaning: an 18th-century English style of chairs and cabinets named after its maker Thomas
a member of a famous troupe of male strip-tease dancers

explanation.definitionFit: The cabinetmaker Thomas gave his name to a furniture style, and the Chippendales are a well-known male dance revue.

clue.text: Composer gets to sing with one of two Spice Girls

parts.note: to hum is to sing with closed lips
the Spice Girls included two Mels, Mel B and Mel C

explanation.surface: A musician gets to perform with a member of the Spice Girls pop group.
explanation.definitionFit: Johann Nepomuk Hummel was an Austrian classical-era pianist and composer.

clue.text: Platform Ten, northbound? Girl is mistaken

indicators.note: northbound in a down clue means read upwards, so the letters go backwards

parts.note: ten is written as the digits 1 and 0, read as the letters I and O

indicators.note: mistaken means wrong, so the word girl appears in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A passenger on Platform Ten for northbound trains turns out to be mistaken about a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Platform Ten' reads as a station platform; Platform is the definition. 'northbound' turns IO into OI; 'is mistaken' turns GIRL into LRIG.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil rig is an offshore drilling platform.

clue.text: Arrangement at university is far from perfect

parts.note: uni is the casual short form of university
a deal is an agreement or arrangement

explanation.surface: Some arrangement agreed at a college turns out to be unsatisfactory.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not ideal falls short of the best.

clue.text: Burden, keeping brother in check

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside, so the check word holds the brother

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain
Fra is the title for an Italian friar or monk, meaning brother

explanation.surface: Something heavy keeps a sibling held back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burden' here is the chorus of a song, an older sense of the word, not a load.
explanation.definitionFit: A song's burden is its recurring chorus, sung again after each verse.

clue.text: Upwardly-mobile industrial financier has hidden talent

indicators.note: Upwardly-mobile says the hidden letters are read backwards
has hidden says the two words contain the letters within them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A socially climbing industrialist conceals a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'has hidden talent' as the definition, but 'has hidden' is the hidden-word indicator. In a down clue 'Upwardly-mobile' reads RIALF upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Flair is a natural gift or aptitude.

clue.text: Fighter happy to carry cane in the wars

indicators.note: to carry means to hold within, so the happy word holds the other letters

parts.note: merry means happy

indicators.note: being in the wars means battered and knocked about, so the word cane is jumbled

explanation.surface: A cheerful soldier is happy to take a walking stick into battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the wars' turns CANE into CENA, and 'to carry' puts it inside MERRY.
explanation.definitionFit: A mercenary is a soldier hired to fight for pay.

clue.text: Friend takes a journey on motorway

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, its 1 read as the letter I
a go can mean a turn or trip, a journey

explanation.surface: A companion sets off for a drive on the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is England's motorway from London to Leeds; crosswords write its 1 as I. 'on' puts GO after MI in an across answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for friend, used informally in English as a pal.

clue.text: Least serious purpose of polygraph, we're told

indicators.note: we're told signals that something heard is meant, so the spelling follows the sound

parts.note: a polygraph is a lie detector, so its purpose is a lie test

explanation.surface: Someone is told what a lie detector is for.
explanation.walkthrough: LIE TEST spoken aloud sounds like the superlative of 'light' in its sense of not weighty.
explanation.definitionFit: Light can mean trivial or frivolous, and the superlative is the most frivolous.

clue.text: Quarrel and refuse to make building blocks

definitions.meaning: an old slang word for a row or squabble
cinders and small ash, the waste mixed with cement to make lightweight blocks

explanation.surface: Someone argues and won't agree to produce bricks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refuse' is the noun (rubbish), not the verb 'decline'.
explanation.definitionFit: Breeze is dated slang for a row, and also the cinders used in breeze blocks.
